newsitem.title: UK: Grand Met to sell Aunt Nellie's to Seneca.
newsitem.headline: Grand Met to sell Aunt Nellie's to Seneca.

text.p: Britain's Grand Metropolitan said on Monday it had agreed to sell its Aunt Nellie's Farm Kitchens division to Seneca Foods for around 15 million stg.
Aunt Nellie's, based in Wisconcin, U.S.A., is a glass-jar fruit and vegetable business operating three plants in the U.S.
Grand Metropolitan said it would take an exceptional charge of 39 million stg from the sale of which 28 million stg was goodwill previously written off.
"The 39 million stg will be taken in the half-year results to be announced on May 15," Grand Met said.
Part of its The Pillsbury Company unit, Aunt Nellie's employed 280 people and its 1996 sales was around $50 million and the business had broken even.
Pillsbury's chief executive Paul Walsh said the sale would improve its return on capital as it was part of the group's strategy to get out of low-return businesses.
